**DonorDock** is generally the better choice if you want a nonprofit CRM focused on **donor management, email, reporting, and retention** in one place, while **Network for Good** is stronger if you want a **fundraising platform with coaching and simple setup** for small nonprofits.[1][5][7]

Here’s the practical difference:

| Category | DonorDock | Network for Good |
|---|---|---|
| **Primary focus** | Donor CRM + marketing tools + fundraising workflows[6][7] | Fundraising software + donor management + coaching[5] |
| **Ease of use** | Frequently described as easy to use and easy to set up[6][7][9] | Also described by users as very user-friendly[1] |
| **Email / communications** | Includes email marketing and donor communications[6][7] | Includes communications tools, but user feedback suggests it can feel limited for outreach[1][5] |
| **Reporting / retention** | Strong emphasis on reports, retention, year-over-year tracking[1][6] | Supports donor management, but appears less focused on deeper CRM-style workflows[1][5] |
| **Pricing/value** | Marketed as more affordable than some competitors and includes many features in one plan[6] | Positioned as an all-in-one platform for small and midsize nonprofits, but pricing details were not provided in the results[5] |
| **Best fit** | Organizations wanting a more complete CRM and engagement system[6][7][9] | Small nonprofits wanting simple fundraising with built-in guidance[5] |

A few important clarifications:

- **Network for Good** now appears as part of **Bonterra**, and Bonterra describes it as an all-in-one fundraising platform for small and midsize nonprofits.[5]
- The term **Network for Good** is also used for a **donor-advised fund / nonprofit disbursement entity** in some contexts, which is separate from the software product history.[2][3][4]
- User reviews in the provided results suggest **DonorDock is stronger for organized donor tracking and engagement**, while **Network for Good is praised for simplicity but criticized as limited for broader outreach needs**.[1]

If you tell me your nonprofit size and what matters most—**pricing, CRM depth, email marketing, fundraising pages, or ease of setup**—I can recommend the better fit more specifically.
